text: Question: A 45-year-old female client arrived at the outpatient clinic for an annual physical examination. Which of the following would be most advisable for the nurse to continue to monitor?
A. Nutrition status.
B. Peripheral vision.
C. Bone composition.
D. Urinary incontinence.

notes: Rationale:

Not correct:
• “Nutrition status.” – General screening, not the source priority
• “Bone composition.” – Bone loss matters but is not the keyed focus
• “Urinary incontinence.” – Not an expected universal finding

slides.title: A nurse is educating a client on the effects of immobility. Which of the followi
text: Question: A nurse is educating a client on the effects of immobility. Which of the following, if stated by the patient, indicates they needs additional teaching?
A. I may experience more frequent UTI’s
B. I may experience pooling of respiratory secretions
C. I may develop diarrhea which can lead to skin breakdown
D. I may experience stiff joints or contractures
Correct answer: C. I may develop diarrhea which can lead to skin breakdown
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• I may develop diarrhea which can lead to skin breakdown
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “I may develop diarrhea which can lead to skin breakdown” – Constipation is more typical
Not correct:
• “I may experience more frequent UTI’s” – Urinary stasis increases infection risk
• “I may experience pooling of respiratory secretions” – Reduced mobility impairs secretion clearance
• “I may experience stiff joints or contractures” – Disuse promotes contractures
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 4 - Basic Care & Comfort, slide 42: “Slow peristalsis”
Slow peristalsis (constipation), not diarrhea, is listed as an effect of immobility.

text: Question: A nurse is providing nail care for a non-diabetic client. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
A. Clean under the nail with an orange stick
B. File the nails in a rounded shape.
C. Push the cuticles back with a metal nail file.
D. Trim the nails at the lateral corners.
Correct answer: A. Clean under the nail with an orange stick
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:

• Clean under the nail with an orange stick

Not correct:
• “File the nails in a rounded shape.” – Rounded toenail edges risk ingrowth
• “Push the cuticles back with a metal nail file.” – Can injure cuticles
• “Trim the nails at the lateral corners.” – Cutting corners risks ingrowth

text: Question: A nurse is changing a client's bed linens. Which action, if observed, requires follow up by the preceptor?
A. The nurse puts on gloves and a gown before removing bed sheets.
B. The nurse makes sure the call-light is in reach before leaving the room.
C. The nurse puts all 4 side rails up prior to leaving the room.
D. The nurse places the draw under the client’s hips for transfer.
Correct answer: C. The nurse puts all 4 side rails up prior to leaving the room.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The nurse puts all 4 side rails up prior to leaving the room.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The nurse puts all 4 side rails up prior to leaving the room.” – May constitute a restraint
Not correct:
• “The nurse puts on gloves and a gown before removing bed sheets.” – PPE protects against anticipated contamination
• “The nurse makes sure the call-light is in reach before leaving the room.” – Maintains access to assistance
• “The nurse places the draw under the client’s hips for transfer.” – Draw sheet aids repositioning
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 4 - Basic Care & Comfort, slide 62: “Raise 2 side rails up”
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 4 (B).

text: Question: A nurse is assessing a group of clients for those at risk for falls. Which of the following clients is most at risk?
A. The 30 y.o. male client receiving IV narcotics every 2hrs.
B. The 80 y.o. client who had a stroke with left sided weakness and urinary frequency.
C. The 25 y.o. client who had a spinal fusion who is completely reliant on staff to turn and reposition.
D. The 72 y.o. client taking a beta blocker that is causing orthostatic hypotension.
Correct answer: B. The 80 y.o. client who had a stroke with left sided weakness and urinary frequency.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The 80 y.o. client who had a stroke with left sided weakness and urinary frequency.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The 80 y.o. client who had a stroke with left sided weakness and urinary frequency.” – Weakness, age and urgency compound risk
Not correct:
• “The 30 y.o. male client receiving IV narcotics every 2hrs.” – Sedation increases risk, but fewer listed factors
• “The 25 y.o. client who had a spinal fusion who is completely reliant on staff to turn a…” – Dependent mobility limits independent attempts
• “The 72 y.o. client taking a beta blocker that is causing orthostatic hypotension.” – Orthostasis is a risk, but fewer listed factors
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: After instruction, which actions by a patient who can bear weight on both feet b
text: Question: After instruction, which actions by a patient who can bear weight on both feet but has left-side weakness indicates an understand of the proper use of a walker?
A. The patient steps forward with the right leg and then moves the walker forward.
B. The patient moves the walker and the left leg forward at the same time, then takes a step with the right leg forward.
C. The patient steps forward with the left leg and then moves the walker forward.
D. The patient moves the walker and the right leg forward at the same time, then takes a step with the left leg forward.
Correct answer: B. The patient moves the walker and the left leg forward at the same time, then takes a step with the right leg forward.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The patient moves the walker and the left leg forward at the same time, then takes a step with the right leg forward.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The patient moves the walker and the left leg forward at the same time, then takes a st…” – Supports weaker leg before strong leg
Not correct:
• “The patient steps forward with the right leg and then moves the walker forward.” – Walker should lead
• “The patient steps forward with the left leg and then moves the walker forward.” – Weak leg advances without support
• “The patient moves the walker and the right leg forward at the same time, then takes a s…” – Incorrect leg sequence
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: While using crutches the client moves both crutches forward and then moves both
text: Question: While using crutches the client moves both crutches forward and then moves both legs forward past the placement of the crutches. This is known as the
A. Two-point gait
B. Swing-through-gait
C. Three-point gait
D. Swing-to-gait
Correct answer: B. Swing-through-gait
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Swing-through-gait
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)

• “Swing-through-gait” – Both legs pass crutches
Not correct:
• “Two-point gait” – Opposite crutch and foot alternate
• “Three-point gait” – Affected leg and crutches advance then strong leg
• “Swing-to-gait” – Legs advance only to crutches

text: Question: The nurse has performed a health assessment of a client who has had a bowel movement which is green in color.  The nurse is aware that a green bowel movement is often an indication of
A. gallbladder infection.
B. liver infection.
C. pancreatic infection.
D. intestinal infection.
Correct answer: D. intestinal infection.
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• intestinal infection.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “intestinal infection.” – Rapid transit may cause green stool; nonspecific
Not correct:
• “gallbladder infection.” – More often associated with impaired bile flow
• “liver infection.” – May cause pale stools with cholestasis
• “pancreatic infection.” – Malabsorption may cause fatty stools

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a patient who will begin taking atenolol. What informati
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a patient who will begin taking atenolol. What information will the nurse include when teaching the patient about taking this medication?
A. The patient must rise slowly from a chair or bed.
B. Use NSAIDs as needed for mild to moderate pain.
C. The medication is safe to take during pregnancy.
D. The drug must be taken twice daily.
Correct answer: A. The patient must rise slowly from a chair or bed.

notes: Rationale:

• The patient must rise slowly from a chair or bed.

• “The patient must rise slowly from a chair or bed.” – Reduces orthostatic symptoms
Not correct:
• “Use NSAIDs as needed for mild to moderate pain.” – NSAIDs may blunt BP control
• “The medication is safe to take during pregnancy.” – Potential fetal risk; requires review
• “The drug must be taken twice daily.” – Frequency depends on prescription
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 8 - Cardiac, slide 5: “Dangle from supine to standing”

text: Question: The nurse administers subcutaneous epinephrine to a patient who is experiencing an anaphylactic reaction. The nurse should expect to monitor the patient for which symptom?
A. Bradycardia
B. Decreased urinary output
C. Nausea and vomiting
D. Hypotension
Correct answer: B. Decreased urinary output
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Decreased urinary output
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Decreased urinary output” – Vasoconstriction may decrease renal perfusion
Not correct:
• “Bradycardia” – Epinephrine usually increases heart rate
• “Nausea and vomiting” – Possible but not the keyed perfusion concern
• “Hypotension” – Usually raises blood pressure

text: Question: The nurse is preparing to administer bethanechol to a patient who is experiencing urinary retention. The nurse notes that the patient has a blood pressure of 90/60 mm Hg and a heart rate of 98 beats per minute. The nurse will perform which action?
A. Hold the medication and notify the provider of the decreased blood pressure.
B. Administer the drug and monitor urine output.
C. Give the medication and notify the provider of the increased heart rate.
D. Administer the medication and monitor vital signs frequently.
Correct answer: A. Hold the medication and notify the provider of the decreased blood pressure.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Hold the medication and notify the provider of the decreased blood pressure.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Hold the medication and notify the provider of the decreased blood pressure.” – Low BP may worsen with bethanechol
Not correct:
• “Administer the drug and monitor urine output.” – Unsafe to give with hypotension
• “Give the medication and notify the provider of the increased heart rate.” – Increased pulse does not justify giving
• “Administer the medication and monitor vital signs frequently.” – Monitoring does not prevent worsening hypotension
